entry.title: S/4HANA Cloud Public–Cost deferral (EBRR) on non-billable service order items linked to a contract
entry.content:
Hello experts,

we are implementing SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (Service Order Management 3D2, Service Contract Management 3MO, Event-Based Revenue Recognition – Service Documents 3M3). We are trying to solve a cost deferral requirement and would appreciate any advice or experience.

Business context

Our customer performs cyclic and extraordinary maintenance on machines.

  • Billing is done from the service contract using an ad-hoc billing plan, typically a down payment (e.g. 75%) when work is completed, and the final invoice in the following quarter.
  • Service orders are used only to collect costs: stock materials issued (service part items), purchased materials/services, and internal labor hours coming from an external system. The service order items are not billable and the service orders reference the service contract.

Requirement

Costs posted on the service orders must not be recognized immediately. They must be deferred and recognized only at final billing, together with the related revenue. In other words, we need costs and revenue to be matched: costs on the service order, revenue on the referenced contract.

What we observe in the standard

  1. Non-billable service order items: costs are recognized immediately. We set the recognition key CCOCC (Completed Contract – Service Order) manually on the non-billable item in the app Revenue Recognition (Event-Based) – Service Documents before the goods issue. The goods issue cost was still recognized immediately (no COS adjustment, no Deferred COS).
  2. Key derivation: in the SSCUI Derivation of Recognition Key for Service Documents (102968) we cannot enter the non-billable item category. It seems only billing-relevant item categories are allowed.
  3. Billable item with zero value (workaround): if we add a billable item with value 0 and CCOCC, the deferral works as expected: Actual Cost 135, COS Adjustment –135, Deferred COS 135. However:
    1. the job Schedule Technical Completion for Financial Close does not set TECO, with the warning: “Invoices must be created for the item and posted to financial accounting. Status of the account assignment object stays Released.”
    2. this item will never be invoiced (billing is done from the contract), so the costs would remain deferred indefinitely;
    3. creating a zero-value invoice just to reach TECO is not acceptable for fiscal reasons (Italian e-invoicing / SdI, tax postings, fiscal numbering)
  4. Financial hierarchy with service contract as root item: this seems to be exactly the intended solution, since service order costs are collected on the contract item where revenue is. However, as far as we understand it requires a dedicated contract item category with the flag “Root Item in Financial Hierarchy”. We cannot create new item categories in our Public Cloud tenant, and we are not sure whether the scenario is available in Public Cloud at all.

Billable item with zero value (workaround): how we can recognized the costs without the invoice?

Billable item with billing status completed: standard behavior after the invoicing.

Questions

  1. Is there a standard way in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to defer costs on non-billable service order items referencing a billable service contract, and recognize them when the contract is billed?
  2. Is the financial hierarchy with service contract item as root item available in Public Cloud? If so, is there an SAP-delivered contract item category with the root flag, or another way to activate it?
  3. If we keep a billable item that will never be invoiced, is there any standard way to set TECO on it (e.g. a billing status, rejection reason or other setting) so that EBRR releases the deferred costs at period-end closing, without issuing an invoice?
  4. Has anyone faced a similar scenario (contract billing + service order cost collection + cost deferral) in Public Cloud, and how did you solve it?

Thank you in advance for any input!

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
